questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Archimede’s Principle is correct?

options.text: When a body is immersed fully or partially in a fluid, it experiences a downward force that is equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by it.
When a body is immersed fully or partially in a fluid, it experiences an upward force that is equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by it.
When a body is immersed fully or partially in a fluid, it experiences a downward force that is much less than the weight of the fluid displaced by it.
When a body is immersed fully or partially in a fluid, it experiences an upward force that is much less than the weight of the fluid displaced by it.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**When a body is immersed fully or partially in a fluid, it experiences an upward force that is equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by it.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Archimedes' Principle** states that when a body is fully or partially submerged in a fluid (liquid or gas), it experiences an **upward buoyant force**. This force is equal to the **weight of the fluid displaced** by the body.
 
• The upward force, commonly referred to as the **buoyant force**, acts in the opposite direction of gravity and is responsible for the floating or sinking of objects in fluids.
 
• This principle explains why some objects float while others sink. If the **weight of the displaced fluid** is greater than or equal to the weight of the object, the object will float. Otherwise, it will sink.
 
• The principle is widely used in designing ships, submarines, hot air balloons, and other engineering applications where buoyancy is a critical factor.
 
• The formula used in Archimedes' Principle is: Buoyant Force (Fb) = Weight of Displaced

questions.question: If resistors are connected in series, the total or equivalent resistance is ________.

options.text: Always less than any single resistor

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sum of individual resistances**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• When **resistors are connected in series**, the total or equivalent resistance is the **sum of all individual resistances** in the circuit.
 
• The formula to calculate the total resistance in a series circuit is: **Rₜₒₜₐₗ = R₁ + R₂ + R₃ + ... + Rₙ**, where R₁, R₂, R₃, etc., are the resistances of individual resistors.
 
• This is because, in a series connection, the **current remains the same** across all resistors, but the **voltage drop adds up** across each resistor.
 
• The concept of adding resistances in series ensures that the total resistance is always **greater than any individual resistance**.
 
• The series connection is commonly use

questions.question:
A smooth ball is resting on an ideal frictionless plane inclined on both sides. The ball is released from the left and the angle of right plane inclination is small in Case-I and zero in Case-II (flat). The ball travels _________ compared to the equally inclined case.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/52cc5e454003da0272341faed77d4a1f307c302590950af587ac4bcc2f60a0f4.png]

options.text: equal distance in Case-I and farther distance in Case-II
equal distance in Case-I and moves forever in Case-II
farther distance in Case-I and moves forever in Case-II
small distance in Case-I and equal distance in Case-II

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3: farther distance in Case-I and moves forever in Case-II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Case-I: Inclined Plane with Small Angle**: In Case-I, the ball is released from a plane inclined on the left and rolls onto a plane inclined on the right, but with a smaller angle. The smaller angle on the right reduces the slope, thereby extending the rolling distance before the ball comes to a stop. *Hence, the ball travels farther compared to an equally inclined case.*
 
• **Case-II: Flat Surface (Zero Inclination)**: When the ball transitions from the inclined plane on the left to a flat surface on the right, there is no opposing force to stop its motion. Since the plane is frictionless, the ball continues to move indefinitely due to the absence of friction or any other resisting force. *Hence, the ball moves forever.*
 
• **Comparison with Equally Inclined Case**: In an equally inclined scenario, the ball's motion would be symmetrical, and the ball would stop at an equal distance on both sides due to gravity's equal opposing forces. Case-I modifies this condition, causing the ball to travel farther on the smaller inclined plane. Case-II, with no inclination, eliminates the stopping mechanism altogether. *Thus, option 3 correctly identifies the outcomes.*
 
• **Physics of Motion on Frictionless Planes**: The ball's behavior is determined solely by gravitational forces and the plane's inclination. A smaller inclination reduces the gravitational component acting against the motion, and a flat surface eliminates it entirely, allowing perpetual motion. *This matches the behavior described in the question.*
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Option 3.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Frictionless Plane:** A frictionless plane is an idealized surface where no resistance opposes the motion of objects. In reality, such surfaces are rare, but they serve as a useful approximation for studying concepts of motion and forces in physics.
 
• **Gravitational Component:** On an inclined plane, the force acting on an object due to gravity can be divided into two components: one parallel to the plane (causing motion) and one perpendicular to the plane (pressing the object against the surface). The parallel component decreases with the angle of inclination.
 
• **Perpetual Motion:** On a frictionless flat surface, an object in motion will continue moving indefinitely according to Newton's First Law of Motion, which states that an object will remain in its state of motion unless acted upon by an external force.
 
• **Inclined Plane Dynamics:** Inclined planes are simple machines that modify the effect of gravity on objects. The steeper the incline, the greater the gravitational force acting to accelerate the object down the slope.
 
• **Practical Applications:** Concepts involving frictionless planes and inclined surfaces are used in designing systems like roller coasters, ramps, and experimental setups in physics labs to study motion and forces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Newton's Laws of Motion:** These laws govern the behavior of objects in motion. In this scenario, Newton's First Law explains why the ball moves forever on a frictionless flat surface, and Newton's Second Law helps calculate the acceleration caused by gravity on the inclined plane.
 
• **Energy Conservation:** The ball's motion on the inclined plane follows the principle of conservation of energy, where potential energy converts to kinetic energy as it rolls down. On a flat surface, the kinetic energy remains constant without losses due to friction.
 
• **Ideal Conditions:** The question assumes ideal conditions like a perfectly smooth ball and frictionless planes, which are theoretical but simplify understanding of motion concepts.
 
• **Real-World Examples:** While frictionless planes are theoretical, low-friction surfaces like ice or air tracks can approximate such conditions and are used in physics experiments.

questions.question: Which of the following observations from Rutherford’s alpha-particle scattering experiment led to the conclusion that most of the atom's volume is empty?

options.text: Some alpha particles were deflected by small angles.
Alpha particles were attracted towards electrons in the atom.
A few alpha particles were deflected by 180°.
Most of the alpha particles passed straight through the gold foil.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Most of the alpha particles passed straight through the gold foil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rutherford's alpha-particle scattering experiment** demonstrated that **most of the alpha particles passed straight through the gold foil**. This indicated that **most of the atom's volume is empty space**, as the particles encountered no obstruction.
 
• The alpha particles, which are positively charged helium nuclei, moved through the gold foil without significant deflection because the atomic structure is largely empty.
 
• **A few alpha particles were deflected at small angles**, which suggested the presence of a positive charge in the atom but did not affect the conclusion that most of the atom is empty space.
 
• **Very few alpha particles were deflected by 180°**, indicating a highly concentrated and positively charged nucleus at the center of the atom. However, the rarity of this event further supported the notion that the atom's interior is mostly empty.
 
• The experiment disproved the earlier "plum pudding model" of the atom, which suggested that positive and negative charges were distributed evenly throughout the atom.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rutherford's Experiment Details:**

 
 
• Conducted by **Ernest Rutherford in 1911**, the experiment involved bombarding a thin gold foil with alpha particles emitted from a radioactive source.
 
• A **fluorescent screen** was used to detect the scattering of alpha particles.
 
• The experiment provided evidence for the nuclear model of the atom, replacing J.J. Thomson's plum pudding model.
 
 
 
• **Structure of the Atom:**
 
 
• The atom consists of a **dense, positively charged nucleus** at its center, containing protons and neutrons.
 
• Electrons, which are negatively charged, revolve around the nucleus in defined orbits.
 
• Most of the atom's volume is empty space, as evidenced by the large fraction of alpha particles passing through the foil without deflection.
 
 
 
• **Key Observations from the Experiment:**
 
 
• Most alpha particles passed straight through the foil, indicating empty space in the atom.
 
• A small fraction of alpha particles were deflected at small angles, suggesting the presence of a dense positive charge.
 
• A very few particles rebounded back, confirming the existence of a concentrated nucleus.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Experiment:**
 
 
• It led to the development of the **nuclear model of the atom**, which forms the basis of modern atomic theory.
 
• The discovery of the nucleus paved the way for further research into subatomic particles, such as protons, neutrons, and later electrons.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Alpha Particles:**

 
 
• Alpha particles are **helium nuclei**, consisting of 2 protons and 2 neutrons, with a positive charge.
 
• Their high energy and positive charge made them suitable for the scattering experiment.
 
 
 
• **Gold Foil:**
 
 
• The gold foil used in the experiment was extremely thin, about **0.00004 cm** thick.
 
• Gold was chosen because it is malleable and can be beaten into very thin sheets.
 
 
 
• **Nucleus Characteristics:**
 
 
• The nucleus occupies a very small volume of the atom (**approximately 1/10,000th** of the atom's diameter).
 
• It contains nearly all the atom's mass and is positively charged.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Experiment:**
 
 
• It confirmed the existence of a nucleus and laid the foundation for the **Bohr model of the atom**.
 
• The findings eventually contributed to the development of quantum mechanics and nuclear physics.

questions.question: Propanone belongs to which homologous series?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ketone**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Propanone**, commonly known as acetone, belongs to the **ketone group**. Ketones are organic compounds characterized by the presence of a carbonyl group (**C=O**) bonded to two carbon atoms.
 
• The chemical formula of propanone is **CH3COCH3**, where the carbonyl group is bonded to two methyl groups.
 
• Ketones are a part of a larger class of organic compounds known as **carbonyl compounds**, which include aldehydes and carboxylic acids.
 
• Propanone is the simplest ketone and is widely used as a **solvent** in industries for applications such as nail polish remover and cleaning agents.
 
• The distinguishing feature of ketones is that the carbonyl group is not bonded to a hydrogen atom, which differentiates them from aldehydes where the carbonyl group is bonded to at least one hydrogen atom.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Alcohol:**

 
 
• Alcohols are organic compounds containing one or more hydroxyl groups (**-OH**) attached to a saturated carbon atom.
 
• Examples include ethanol (**C2H5OH**) and methanol (**CH3OH**).
 
• Alcohols are classified into primary, secondary, and tertiary alcohols based on the number of carbon atoms attached to the carbon holding the hydroxyl group.
 
 
 
• **Aldehyde:**
 
 
• Aldehydes are characterized by the presence of a carbonyl group (**C=O**) bonded to at least one hydrogen atom.
 
• An example is formaldehyde (**HCHO**), which is used in disinfectants and preservatives.
 
• Aldehydes have a distinct odor and are commonly found in flavoring agents and perfumes.
 
 
 
• **Ester:**
 
 
• Esters are organic compounds formed by the reaction of an alcohol and an acid, with the elimination of water.
 
• They contain the functional group **-COOR**, where R is an alkyl or aryl group.
 
• Esters are widely used in perfumes, flavorings, and as solvents in industries.
 
 
 
• **Ketones:**
 
 
• Ketones are used as solvents in industries for applications such as cleaning agents, paint thinners, and nail polish removers.
 
• They are also precursors in the synthesis of various compounds, including pharmaceuticals.
 
• Propanone (acetone) is a well-known example and is widely used due to its effectiveness as a solvent.
 
• Ketones are produced naturally in the human body during fat metabolism in the form of ketone bodies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Propanone (Acetone):**

 
 
• Propanone is highly volatile and flammable, making it suitable for use in laboratory and industrial processes.
 
• It is miscible with water and many organic solvents, making it a versatile solvent.
 
• The chemical structure of propanone is planar due to the sp2 hybridization of the carbonyl carbon.
 
• Propanone plays a role in the pharmaceutical industry as a precursor in drug synthesis.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Ketones:**
 
 
• Ketones are used in the production of plastics and synthetic fibers.
 
• They are intermediates in the synthesis of perfumes, dyes, and explosives.
 
• Ketones serve as solvents for paints, varnishes, and adhesives.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly defines the principal axis of a spherical mirror?

options.text: The line passing through the focus and object
The line passing through the centre of curvature and pole
The perpendicular line drawn from the pole

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The line passing through the centre of curvature and pole.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The principal axis** of a spherical mirror is defined as the **straight line** that passes through the **centre of curvature (C)** and the **pole (P)** of the mirror.
 
• This line acts as the **reference line** for all measurements and is perpendicular to the surface of the spherical mirror at the pole.
 
• The principal axis is significant because it determines the **symmetry** of the mirror and is the axis along which the mirror's properties, such as focus and curvature, are defined.
 
• In both **concave and convex mirrors**, the principal axis is the central line that helps in locating key points like the **focus (F)** and the centre of curvature (C).
 
• Hence, the correct definition of the principal axis is **the line passing through the centre of curvature and pole**, making **Option 2**__ the right answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pole (P):**

 
 
• The pole is the **geometric center** of the mirror's reflecting surface.
 
• It is the point where the **principal axis** intersects the mirror's surface.
 
 
 
• **Centre of Curvature (C):**
 
 
• The centre of curvature is the center of the **sphere** of which the spherical mirror is a part.
 
• It lies outside the mirror for both concave and convex mirrors and is located on the principal axis.
 
 
 
• **Focus (F):**
 
 
• The focus is the point on the principal axis where **parallel rays** of light, after reflection, converge (in concave mirrors) or appear to diverge from (in convex mirrors).
 
• The distance from the pole to the focus is called the **focal length (f)**.
 
 
 
• **Radius of Curvature (R):**
 
 
• The radius of curvature is the distance between the **pole** and the **centre of curvature**.
 
• It is equal to twice the focal length, i.e., **R = 2f**.
 
 
 
• **Convex vs. Concave Mirrors:**
 
 
• **Concave mirrors** are converging mirrors that reflect light inward, while **convex mirrors** are diverging mirrors that spread light outward.
 
• The principal axis remains the same in both types, helping locate key points like the focus and the centre of curvature.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option 1:** "The line passing through the focus and object" is incorrect because the principal axis does not depend on the object's position.
 
• **Option 3:** "The tangent at the pole" is incorrect as a tangent is a line that touches the surface at one point and does not represent the principal axis.
 
• **Option 4:** "The perpendicular line drawn from the pole" is vague and does not define the axis passing through the centre of curvature.
 
• Always remember, the principal axis is the line that passes through the **centre of curvature** and the **pole** of the mirror.

questions.question: What is an ion in chemistry?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A charged atom or molecule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• An **ion** is a particle, atom, or molecule that carries a net electrical charge due to the loss or gain of electrons. This charge can be either positive (cation) or negative (anion).
 
• **Cations** are positively charged ions formed when an atom or molecule loses electrons. Example: Na⁺ (Sodium ion).
 
• **Anions** are negatively charged ions formed when an atom or molecule gains electrons. Example: Cl⁻ (Chloride ion).
 
• Ions play a crucial role in **chemical reactions**, particularly in ionic bonding and electrochemical processes.

questions.question: Three resistors of 4 Omega , 8 Omega , and 12 Omega are connected in series across a 12 {V} battery. The current in the circuit is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.5 A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given resistors of **4 Ω, 8 Ω, and 12 Ω** are connected in **series**. In a series connection, the total or equivalent resistance is the sum of the individual resistances.
 
• The formula to calculate the total resistance in a series circuit is:

 **Rₜₒₜₐₗ = R₁ + R₂ + R₃**.

 Substituting the given values:

 **Rₜₒₜₐₗ = 4 Ω + 8 Ω + 12 Ω = 24 Ω**.
 
• The circuit is powered by a **12 V battery**. Using Ohm's Law, which is **V = IR**, we can calculate the current in the circuit. Rearranging the formula:

 **I = V / R**.
 
• Substitute the values for voltage and total resistance:

 **I = 12 V / 24 Ω = 0.5 A**.
 
• Thus, the current in the circuit is **0.5 A**, which matches the given correct option.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ohm's Law:**

 
 
• **Ohm's Law** states that the current (I) through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage (V) across the two points and inversely proportional to the resistance (R) of the conductor.
 
• The formula is expressed as: **V = IR**, where V is voltage, I is current, and R is resistance.
 
• This law is fundamental in understanding the behavior of electrical circuits.
 
 
 
• **Series Circuit:**
 
 
• In a series circuit, the current remains the same across all components, but the voltage is divided among them.
 
• The total resistance in a series circuit is the sum of all individual resistances: **Rₜₒₜₐₗ = R₁ + R₂ + ... + Rₙ**.
 
 
 
• **Resistors in Series vs. Parallel:**
 
 
• In a series connection, resistors add up to increase the total resistance, while in a parallel connection, the total resistance decreases.
 
• The formula for total resistance in a parallel circuit is:

 **1/Rₜₒₜₐₗ = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + ... + 1/Rₙ**.
 
 
 
• **Electric Current:**
 
 
• Electric current is the rate of flow of electric charge through a conductor.
 
• The unit of electric current is the **ampere (A)**, named after French physicist André-Marie Ampère.
 
• 1 ampere is equivalent to 1 coulomb of charge passing through a point in 1 second.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Power in an Electrical Circuit:**

 
 
• The power (P) dissipated in an electrical circuit is calculated using the formula: **P = VI**, where V is voltage and I is current.
 
• For resistors, power can also be expressed as: **P = I²R** or **P = V²/R**.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Series Circuits:**
 
 
• Series circuits are commonly used in applications where the same current is required to flow through multiple components, such as decorative lights.
 
• However, if one component in the series circuit fails, the entire circuit is interrupted.
 
 
 
• **Units of Measurement:**
 
 
• **Voltage:** Measured in volts (V).
 
• **Resistance:** Measured in ohms (Ω).
 
• **Current:** Measured in amperes (A).

questions.question: Which of the following substances have a high chance of contributing to the phenomenon of biological magnification?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pesticide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pesticides** are chemical substances used to eliminate or control pests in agricultural practices. These include herbicides, insecticides, fungicides, and rodenticides.
 
• Pesticides are non-biodegradable and persist in the environment, leading to their accumulation in the food chain. This process is termed **biological magnification**, where concentrations increase as one moves up the trophic levels.
 
• The phenomenon of biological magnification is particularly harmful as it affects organisms at the top of the food chain, such as humans, by causing severe health risks like **cancer, neurological disorders, and reproductive issues**.
 
• Other organic substances like **rose petals, neem bark, and orange peel** do not contribute to biological magnification as they are biodegradable and decompose naturally in the environment. Hence, these are *incorrect options.*
 
• Examples of pesticides that cause biological magnification include **DDT, Aldrin, Heptachlor, and Mercury-based compounds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Biological Magnification:**

 
 
• **Definition:** Biological magnification refers to the increase in concentration of toxic substances, such as pesticides or heavy metals, as they move up the food chain.
 
• **Impact:** Organisms at higher trophic levels, such as predatory birds, fish, and humans, accumulate higher concentrations of toxins, leading to severe ecological and health impacts.
 
• **Examples:** Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs) like **DDT** and mercury compounds are common substances involved in magnification.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true?

options.text: Power and work are independent of each other.
More work done in less time means more power.
Work done does not affect power.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**More work done in less time means more power.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Power** is defined as the rate at which work is done or energy is transferred over time. The formula for power is: **Power = Work Done / Time**.
 
• When **more work is done in less time**, the numerator (work done) increases while the denominator (time) decreases, resulting in a higher value of power. ***Hence, this statement is correct.***
 
• **Statement 1:** Power and work are not independent of each other, as power is directly dependent on the amount of work done and the time taken. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 2:** Power does not necessarily decrease when work increases. If the time remains constant or decreases, power will increase. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 4:** Work done directly affects power as they are mathematically related. Power increases when work increases, provided time remains constant or decreases. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Power:**

 
 
• Power is measured in **Watts (W)**, where 1 Watt equals 1 Joule of work done per second.
 
• Power can also be expressed in terms of energy transfer: **Power = Energy Transferred / Time**.
 
 
 
• **Work:**
 
 
• Work is defined as the product of force and displacement in the direction of the force: **Work = Force × Displacement × cos(θ)**, where θ is the angle between force and displacement.
 
• Work is measured in **Joules (J)**.
 
 
 
• **Time:**
 
 
• Time is a crucial parameter in determining power. A shorter time for the same amount of work results in higher power output.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Power:**
 
 
• A 60-Watt bulb consumes 60 Joules of energy per second.
 
• A car engine with a power rating of 100 horsepower (~74600 Watts) does more work in a shorter time compared to a less powerful engine.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Relation Between Power, Work, and Time:**

 
 
• If **work increases** and time remains constant, power increases proportionally.
 
• If work remains constant but **time decreases**, power also increases.
 
 
 
• **Units of Power:**
 
 
• The SI unit of power is the Watt (W).
 
• Other units include horsepower (1 HP = 746 W) and kilowatts (1 kW = 1000 W).
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications:**
 
 
• In mechanical systems, power ratings determine the efficiency of machines, such as engines and motors.
 
• In electrical systems, power ratings indicate energy consumption, as seen in household appliances like air conditioners and refrigerators.

questions.question: What type of solution causes water to move out of a cell through the plasma membrane, making the cell shrink?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hypertonic solution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **hypertonic solution** is one where the concentration of solutes outside the cell is higher than inside the cell. This difference in solute concentration creates an osmotic gradient.
 
• When a cell is placed in a hypertonic solution, **water moves out of the cell** through the plasma membrane via osmosis to balance the solute concentration. This results in the cell shrinking, a process known as **crenation** in animal cells.
 
• The movement of water occurs because of the principle of **osmosis**, where water flows from a region of lower solute concentration to a region of higher solute concentration.
 
• The shrinkage of the cell due to water loss can disrupt its normal functions and, in extreme cases, lead to cell death.
 
• Hypertonic solutions are commonly used in medical treatments, such as reducing edema or managing certain infections, but they must be administered carefully to avoid cellular damage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hypotonic Solution:**

 
 
• A hypotonic solution has a **lower solute concentration** outside the cell compared to the inside.
 
• In such a solution, water moves into the cell, causing it to swell and potentially burst in a process called **lysis**.
 
• Hypotonic solutions are often used in treatments where hydration of cells is required, such as in patients suffering from severe dehydration.
 
 
 
• **Isotonic Solution:**
 
 
• An isotonic solution has an **equal concentration of solutes** inside and outside the cell, resulting in no net movement of water.
 
• Isotonic conditions are ideal for maintaining cell shape and function, and such solutions are commonly used in intravenous fluids like saline (0.9% NaCl).
 
 
 
• **Osmosis:**
 
 
• Osmosis is the movement of water molecules across a **semipermeable membrane** from a region of low solute concentration to a region of high solute concentration.
 
• This process is critical for maintaining cellular homeostasis and plays a key role in various physiological processes.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Hypertonic Solutions:**
 
 
• Hypertonic saline solutions are used in medical treatments to reduce **intracranial pressure** or treat pulmonary edema.
 
• In food preservation, hypertonic solutions like concentrated sugar or salt are used to prevent microbial growth by drawing water out of cells.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Cellular Effects of Different Solutions:**

 
 
• In a **hypertonic solution**, cells shrink (crenation in animal cells, plasmolysis in plant cells).
 
• In a **hypotonic solution**, cells swell and may burst (lysis in animal cells, turgidity in plant cells).
 
• In an **isotonic solution**, cells maintain their normal size and shape.
 
 
 
• **Osmoregulation:**
 
 
• Organisms regulate water and solute concentrations to prevent damage caused by hypertonic, hypotonic, or isotonic conditions.
 
• For example, freshwater organisms actively expel excess water, while marine organisms regulate salt intake to maintain balance.
 
 
 
• **Medical Implications:**
 
 
• Understanding the effects of hypertonic, hypotonic, and isotonic solutions is critical in administering intravenous (IV) fluids to patients.
 
• Incorrect use of these solutions can lead to severe conditions like cellular dehydration or swelling.

questions.question: The angle between the incident ray and the emergent ray from a prism is called __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Angle of deviation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **angle of deviation** is defined as the angle between the direction of the incident ray and the direction of the emergent ray as it exits a prism.
 
• When a light ray passes through a prism, it undergoes **refraction twice**: once when it enters the prism and once when it exits the prism. This bending of light results in the angle of deviation.
 
• The magnitude of the angle of deviation depends on factors like the **angle of incidence**, the **refractive index** of the material of the prism, and the **apex angle** of the prism.
 
• For a given prism, there is a specific angle of incidence at which the angle of deviation is minimum. This is called the **minimum deviation angle**, and it is often used to calculate the refractive index of the prism.
 
• It is an important concept in optics and is widely studied in the context of prism-based dispersion and light refraction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Angle of Prism:**

 
 
• The **angle of prism** refers to the angle between the two refracting surfaces of the prism. It is also known as the **apex angle**.
 
• The angle of prism plays a significant role in determining the extent of deviation of light passing through the prism.
 
 
 
• **Angle of Incidence:**
 
 
• The **angle of incidence** is the angle between the incident ray and the normal to the surface at the point of incidence.
 
• This angle affects the refraction of light and consequently influences the angle of deviation in a prism.
 
 
 
• **Critical Angle:**
 
 
• The **critical angle** is the angle of incidence above which total internal reflection occurs for light traveling from a denser to a rarer medium.
 
• It is not directly related to the angle of deviation but is a key concept in understanding refraction and reflection phenomena.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Angle of Deviation:**
 
 
• It is used in the design of optical instruments like spectrometers to measure the refractive index of materials.
 
• The concept is also applied in the study of dispersion, where light is separated into its constituent colors using a prism.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Light Dispersion:**

 
 
• The angle of deviation is responsible for the splitting of white light into its constituent colors when it passes through a prism. This phenomenon is called **dispersion**.
 
• The deviation angle is different for different wavelengths of light, which leads to the formation of a spectrum.
 
 
 
• **Minimum Deviation:**
 
 
• At minimum deviation, the refracted ray inside the prism is symmetric with respect to the prism's base, and the path of light is at its most efficient.
 
• This condition is often used in experiments to determine the refractive index of the prism material.

questions.question: The frequency of a sound wave is 250 Hz. What is its time period?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.004 s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **time period** of a wave is the reciprocal of its frequency. It is calculated using the formula:

 **Time Period (T) = 1 / Frequency (f)**
 
• The given frequency of the sound wave is **250 Hz**.

 Substituting this into the formula:

 **T = 1 / 250 = 0.004 seconds**.
 
• Therefore, the time period of the sound wave is **0.004 seconds**.
 
• The unit of frequency is **Hertz (Hz)**, which represents the number of cycles per second. The unit of time period is **seconds (s)**.
 
• This calculation confirms that the correct option is **0.004 s**, which corresponds to Option 1__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Frequency and Time Period Relationship:**

 
 
• Frequency (**f**) and time period (**T**) are inversely proportional. This means as frequency increases, the time period decreases, and vice versa.
 
• The mathematical expression for their relationship is:

 **T = 1 / f** or **f = 1 / T**.
 
 
 
• **Definition of Frequency:**
 
 
• Frequency is the number of complete oscillations or cycles a wave completes in one second.
 
• It is measured in **Hertz (Hz)**. For example, 1 Hz = 1 cycle per second.
 
 
 
• **Definition of Time Period:**
 
 
• The time period is the time taken to complete one oscillation or cycle of a wave.
 
• It is measured in **seconds (s)**.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Frequency and Time Period:**
 
 
• These concepts are widely used in fields like **acoustics, electronics, and signal processing**.
 
• In sound waves, **frequency determines the pitch** of the sound, while the time period provides insights into the wave's periodicity.
 
 
 
• **Real-life Examples:**
 
 
• A guitar string vibrating at **440 Hz** has a time period of approximately **0.00227 seconds**.
 
• The human ear can typically hear frequencies ranging from **20 Hz to 20,000 Hz**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Speed of Sound:**

 
 
• The speed of sound in air is approximately **343 m/s** at room temperature (20°C).
 
• The speed depends on factors like **medium, temperature, and pressure**.
 
 
 
• **Wavelength and Frequency:**
 
 
• Wavelength (**λ**) is inversely proportional to frequency when the speed of the wave is constant:

 **λ = v / f**, where **v** is the speed of the wave.
 
• Higher frequency waves have shorter wavelengths.
 
 
 
• **Practical Use:**
 
 
• Frequency and time period calculations are vital in designing **musical instruments, speakers, and communication devices**.
 
• They are also crucial in **medical imaging techniques** like ultrasound.

questions.question: A baker sells 100 cupcakes and earns a profit equal to the selling price of 20 cupcakes. What is his profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When profit is equal to the Selling Price (SP) of x items for n items sold:

Profit % = [x ÷ (n − x)] × 100

Profit % = [20 ÷ (100 − 20)] × 100

Profit % = (20 ÷ 80) × 100 = 25%

In decimal form: 25 ÷ 100 = 0.25

**∴ The correct answer is 0.25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Total cupcakes sold = 100, Profit = SP of 20 cupcakes.

Formula: Profit = Selling Price (SP) − Cost Price (CP)

 Total Selling Price (100 units) 
• Cost Price (80 units) Profit (20 units) 
• Base for % Calculation (CP) 

Let the Selling Price (SP) of 1 cupcake = 1 unit.

⇒ Total SP of 100 cupcakes = 100 units.

⇒ Profit = SP of 20 cupcakes = 20 units.

⇒ Cost Price (CP) = SP − Profit

⇒ CP = 100 − 20 = 80 units.

⇒ Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (20 ÷ 80) × 100 = 25%.

⇒ Profit in decimal = 0.25.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit based on Cost Price

If profit is equal to the CP of x items while selling n items, then Profit % = (x ÷ n) × 100.

Loss based on Selling Price

Marked Price (MP)

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price. Selling Price = MP × [1 − (Discount % ÷ 100)].

questions.question: The income of Raman is ₹68,500. He saves 22.5% of his income. If his income increases by 14% and expenditure increases by 40%, then his savings will:

Let Income = 100 units, Savings = 22.5 units, Expenditure = 77.5 units.

Income = ₹68,500, Savings Percentage = 22.5%

Income = Expenditure + Savings

 Income: ₹68,500 (100%) Exp: 77.5% Sav: 22.5%

Percentage change in savings = (Change in Savings ÷ Original Savings) × 100. This helps in identifying the growth or reduction rate.

questions.question: If the price of a product is first increased by 18% and then decreased by 22%. Find the percentage change in the price (correct to two places of decimals).

Where a = first % change | b = second % change

Use + for increase and − for decrease.

 Original ₹100

Successive Percentage Change — Direct Formula

For two successive % changes a and b: Net % = a + b + ab/100. Use + for increase and − for decrease. Example: +20% then −20% ⇒ net = 20 − 20 + (20 × −20)/100 = −4% — always results in a net decrease when same % is applied both ways.

Multiplying Factor Method

x% increase → multiply by (100+x)/100 | x% decrease → multiply by (100−x)/100. For this question: 100 × 118/100 × 78/100 = 92.04. Net factor = 0.9204 ⇒ decrease of 7.96%. This method works for any number of successive changes.

Three Successive % Changes

If price drops by x%, the % increase needed to recover = x/(100−x) × 100. For this question final price is 92.04% of original — to recover: 7.96/92.04 × 100 ≈ 8.65% increase is needed. Recovery % is always greater than the decrease %.

⇒ 4 × (10³ − 6³) = 8² × h

⇒ 4 × (1000 − 216) = 64 × h

questions.question: A train of length 299 m takes 12 seconds to pass another train 101 m long coming from the opposite direction. If the speed of the first train is 71 km/hr, then find the speed of the second train.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance to cover = Sum of lengths of both trains = 299 + 101 = 400 m

Relative speed in m/s = Total distance ÷ Time = 400 ÷ 12 = 100/3 m/s

Relative speed in km/hr = (100/3) × (18/5) = 120 km/hr

In opposite direction, Relative Speed = Speed₁ + Speed₂

Speed₂ = 120 − 71 = 49 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 49 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Length of Train 2 (L₂) = 101 m

Time taken (T) = 12 seconds

Speed of Train 1 (S₁) = 71 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction) = S₁ + S₂

Speed = Distance / Time

To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question: If 20\% of a number is added to 72 , then the result is the same number. 60\% of the same number is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the original number be 100%.

Given: 20% of number + 72 = 100% of number.

⇒ 72 = 100% − 20% = 80%.

⇒ 80% of the number = 72.

⇒ 60% of the number = (72 ÷ 80) × 60 = 0.9 × 60 = 54.

**∴ The correct answer is 54.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

20% of a number added to 72 equals the number itself.

**Formula Used:**

Value = (Percentage ÷ 100) × Number

 20% 80% (Value = 72) 
• Total Number = 100% 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the number be x.

⇒ (20/100) × x + 72 = x

⇒ 0.2x + 72 = x

⇒ 72 = x − 0.2x

⇒ 72 = 0.8x

⇒ x = 72 ÷ 0.8

⇒ x = 90

⇒ 60% of x = (60/100) × 90

⇒ 60% of x = 0.6 × 90 = 54

**∴ The correct answer is 54.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

To solve quickly, convert percentages to fractions: 20% = 1/5, 60% = 3/5, 80% = 4/5. Here, (4/5) × x = 72 gives x = 90.

Base Value Concept

Always identify the 100% base. If a part is given, the remaining part (100% − given%) corresponds to the added or subtracted numerical value.

Successive Percentage Formula

For two successive changes of a% and b%, the net change is [a + b + (a × b)/100]%.

questions.question: Which country’s authorities were flagged by India in 2025 for hybrid cannabis smuggling via couriers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thailand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In early **2025**, Indian drug law enforcement agencies, led by the **Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB)**, flagged **Thailand** as a major source of **hybrid cannabis** being smuggled into the country.
 
• The illicit trade primarily utilizes international **courier services** and the **postal network** to deliver high-potency cannabis "buds" to major Indian metropolitan areas such as **Mumbai**, **Delhi**, and **Bengaluru**.
 
• **Hybrid cannabis** from **Thailand** is specifically targeted due to its high **THC (Tetrahydrocannabinol)** content, which ranges between **15% to 30%**, making it far more potent and expensive than the locally grown variety.
 
• Authorities noted that smugglers often use sophisticated **vacuum-sealed packaging** to evade detection by **K-9 units** and conceal the drugs inside harmless items like **clothing**, **food containers**, or **electronics**. ***Hence, Thailand is the correct answer.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Decriminalization in Thailand**:
 
 
• **Thailand** became the first country in **Asia** to decriminalize cannabis in **June 2022**. This move led to a proliferation of cannabis dispensaries across cities like **Bangkok** and **Phuket**.

questions.question: Who took office as the Deputy Governor of the RBI on 2 April 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Poonam Gupta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dr. Poonam Gupta** officially took office as the **Deputy Governor** of the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** on **2 April 2025**.
 
• She was appointed by the **Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC)** following the recommendations of the **Financial Sector Regulatory Appointments Search Committee (FSRASC)**.
 
• Her appointment is significant as she transitions from her role as the **Director General** of the **National Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER)**, where she was the first woman to lead the institution since its inception in **1956**.
 
• As **Deputy Governor**, she is expected to oversee critical portfolios, likely including the **Monetary Policy Department** and the **Department of Economic and Policy Research**, given her extensive background in macroeconomics.
 
• She succeeds **Michael Debabrata Patra**, who served multiple extended terms as the **Deputy Governor** in charge of monetary policy before his tenure concluded in **2025**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of RBI Leadership**:

 
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India** is governed by a **Central Board of Directors**. The executive leadership consists of one **Governor** and a maximum of **four Deputy Governors**.
 
• The appointments are made under **Section 8** of the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**.
 
• The **Governor** and **Deputy Governors** are appointed for a period not exceeding **five years** and are eligible for reappointment.
 
 
 
• **Profile of Poonam Gupta**:
 
 
• Before joining **NCAER**, she served as a **Lead Economist** at the **World Bank** and held positions at the **International Monetary Fund (IMF)**.
 
• She has been a member of the **Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister (EAC-PM)**, providing insights on fiscal and monetary health.
 
• Her expertise lies in **international finance**, **banking**, and the **Indian economy**, with numerous publications in global economic journals.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Analysis**:
 
 
• **Michael Debabrata Patra**: Served as **Deputy Governor** from **2020** to **2025**. He was a vital member of the **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)** and was known for his hawkish stance on inflation.
 
• **Ashwani Bhatia**: A former **Managing Director** of the **State Bank of India (SBI)**, he later served as a **Whole-Time Member (WTM)** at the **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)**.
 
• **Michael Debroy**: This appears to be a distractor name, potentially conflating **Bibek Debroy** (former Chairman of EAC-PM) and **Michael Patra**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **RBI Headquarters** is located in **Mumbai, Maharashtra**. It was moved from **Kolkata** to **Mumbai** in **1937**.
 
• The **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)** consists of **six members**, including the **Governor** and the **Deputy Governor** in charge of monetary policy, alongside three external members.
 
• The role of the **Deputy Governor** is diverse, ranging from managing the **Foreign Exchange Department** to **Banking Regulation** and **Currency Management** (issuance of **banknotes**).
 
• Historical Significance: While there have been several female **Deputy Governors** in the past (such as **K.J. Udeshi**, **Shyamala Gopinath**, and **Usha Thorat**), the appointment of a specialist from a research background like **Poonam Gupta** continues the tradition of blending lateral entry with internal promotion within the central bank.

questions.question: What are the revised investment caps for Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) in corporate bonds for FY 2025-26, as announced by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in April 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**15%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, in its move to regulate foreign capital inflows, announced the revised investment caps for **Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs)** for the **fiscal year 2025-26** in **April 2025**.
 
• As per the notification, the limit for **FPI investment** in **corporate bonds** has been maintained at **15%** of the outstanding stock of corporate bonds.
 
• This limit is part of the **Medium-Term Framework (MTF)**, which aims to provide a predictable regime for foreign investment in the Indian debt market while ensuring financial stability.
 
• The **RBI** keeps these limits under review to balance the need for attracting **foreign exchange** and managing the volatility associated with **portfolio flows**.
 
• These regulations apply to all **FPIs** registered with the **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)**, ensuring that the total holdings of all foreign investors do not exceed the specified **15%** threshold of the total market value of outstanding corporate debt.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Foreign Portfolio Investment (FPI):** 
 
 
• **FPI** refers to the entry of funds into a country where foreigners deposit money in a country's **bank** or make purchases in the country's **stock and bond markets**.
 
• Unlike **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)**, FPI does not provide the investor with direct control over the assets or the management of the companies.
 
 
 
• **Corporate Bonds:** 
 
 
• These are **debt instruments** issued by private and public corporations to raise **capital** for various purposes, such as business expansion or refinancing existing debt.
 
• In India, the **corporate bond market** is a crucial source of funding for infrastructure and industrial projects, and **FPI participation** provides necessary **liquidity** to this market.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Authority:** 
 
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** and the **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)** jointly manage the framework for foreign investments.
 
• The **RBI** determines the macro-prudential limits (the caps), while **SEBI** manages the registration and operational guidelines for the investors.
 
 
 
• **Voluntary Retention Route (VRR):** 
 
 
• The **VRR** is a separate channel introduced by the **RBI** to encourage FPIs to invest in **debt markets** in India over a longer period.
 
• Investments through **VRR** are exempt from certain regulatory prescriptions, provided the investors voluntarily commit to retaining a required minimum percentage of their **investment** in India for a specific period.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Government Securities (G-Secs):** Apart from corporate bonds, the **RBI** also sets limits for **G-Secs**. Historically, the limit for FPIs in **Central Government Securities** has been around **6%** of the outstanding stock, which is significantly lower than the **15%** allowed for corporate debt.
 
• **State Development Loans (SDLs):** For **SDLs**, the investment limit is typically set at **2%** of the outstanding stock.
 
• **Impact on Economy:** A **15%** cap helps in deepening the **debt market** without making it overly dependent on foreign "hot money," which can be pulled out quickly during global financial crises, leading to **currency depreciation**.
 
• **Fully Accessible Route (FAR):** Certain specified categories of **Government Securities** are opened fully for FPIs without any macro-prudential caps under the **FAR** scheme, which was a major step towards India's inclusion in **global bond indices**.

questions.question: In May 2025, minutes after the PSLV-C61, carrying the earth observation satellite EOS-09, lifted off from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota, the space agency reported a glitch in the _____.

options.text: third stage of the launch vehicle
second stage of the launch vehicle
fourth stage of the launch vehicle
first stage of the launch vehicle

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**third stage of the launch vehicle**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **PSLV-C61** mission, launched in **May 2025**, was intended to place the **EOS-09** satellite into its designated **Sun-Synchronous Polar Orbit**.
 
• Shortly after a successful lift-off from the **Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC)** in **Sriharikota**, **ISRO** (Indian Space Research Organisation) identified a technical glitch specifically in the **third stage (PS3)** of the launch vehicle. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***
 
• The **third stage** of the **PSLV** is critical as it utilizes a **solid rocket motor** to provide the necessary thrust after the vehicle has exited the denser layers of the **Earth's atmosphere**.
 
• Preliminary reports indicated that the anomaly occurred during the **ignition** or **burn phase** of this stage, which hindered the vehicle's ability to reach the required **velocity** for the next phase of the mission.
 
• While the **first** and **second stages** performed nominally, the failure in the **third stage** prevented the **fourth stage** from executing the final **orbital injection**. ***Hence, options 2, 3, and 4 are incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **PSLV (Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle) Structure**:

 
 
• **First Stage (PS1)**: This stage uses a **solid propellant (HTPB)** and is augmented by **strap-on boosters** to provide massive initial thrust.
 
• **Second Stage (PS2)**: This stage employs the **Vikas Engine**, which uses **liquid propellants** (UH25 and N2O4).
 
• **Third Stage (PS3)**: A **solid motor** stage that provides high thrust at high altitudes. It is designed to operate in a **vacuum**.
 
• **Fourth Stage (PS4)**: The uppermost stage of the **PSLV**, comprising two **liquid engines** that are **restartable** to ensure precise satellite placement.
 
 
 
• **EOS-09 (Earth Observation Satellite)**:
 
 
• The **EOS-09** is a high-resolution **imaging satellite** designed for **Earth observation**.
 
• Its primary **applications** include **urban planning**, **agriculture monitoring**, **forestry management**, and **disaster mitigation**.
 
• It was equipped with advanced **optical sensors** to provide data for **cartographic** and **oceanographic** studies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC)**: Located in **Sriharikota**, **Andhra Pradesh**, it is India’s primary **spaceport** responsible for launching **PSLV**, **GSLV**, and **LVM3** missions.
 
• **PSLV Glitches**: Though known as the **Workhorse of ISRO** due to its high success rate, the **PSLV** has occasionally faced challenges, such as the **PSLV-C39** mission failure (heat shield separation issue) and early developmental flight anomalies.
 
• **Mission Analysis**: In the event of a **third-stage glitch**, a **Failure Analysis Committee (FAC)** is typically formed by **ISRO** to investigate the **telemetry data** and identify the root cause, such as **pressure drops** or **propellant exhaustion**.
 
• **Significance of May 2025**: This mission was part of **India's** ongoing effort to enhance its **space-based surveillance** and **remote sensing** capabilities.

• This index is designed as a strategic tool to **evaluate and improve state drug regulatory frameworks** across India. It focuses on creating a competitive yet collaborative environment for states to enhance their oversight of the **pharmaceutical sector**.
 
• The mechanism follows an **open and evidence-based approach**, ensuring that the performance of **State Drug Controller** offices is measured against standardized **benchmarks** and **data-driven metrics**.

questions.question: India joined which European drone programme as an observer in January 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eurodrone**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **January 2025**, **India** officially joined the **Eurodrone** program as an **observer**, marking a significant expansion of its defense cooperation with **European** nations.
 
• The **Eurodrone** is a collaborative project between **Germany**, **France**, **Italy**, and **Spain**, designed to develop an advanced **Medium-Altitude Long-Endurance (MALE)** Remotely Piloted Aircraft System (**RPAS**).
 
• The program is managed by **OCCAR** (Organisation for Joint Armament Co-operation), which acts as the executive agent on behalf of the participating **European** member states.
 
• As an **observer**, **India** will have the opportunity to participate in technical briefings, track the progress of **aerospace** development, and understand the technical standards required for **unmanned aerial systems** in **non-segregated airspace**.
 
• This move is seen as a strategic step for **India** to diversify its **surveillance** and **reconnaissance** capabilities while strengthening the **India-EU** defense and security partnership.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Technical Specifications of Eurodrone:**

 
 
• The **Eurodrone** is notable for its **twin-turboprop engine** configuration, which provides enhanced safety and reliability compared to single-engine platforms.
 
• It is designed for multi-mission capabilities, including **Intelligence, Surveillance, Target Acquisition, and Reconnaissance (ISTAR)**, as well as potential future **combat** applications.
 
• Key industrial partners involved in the project include **Airbus Defence and Space**, **Dassault Aviation**, and **Leonardo**.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Significance for India:**
 
 
• India's **Ministry of Defence** aims to reduce dependence on any single source for **HALE** and **MALE** drones. Currently, India utilizes **Heron** drones from **Israel** and is in the process of inducting **MQ-9B Predator** drones from the **USA**.
 
• The **observer status** allows **DRDO** and Indian **aerospace** experts to gain insights into **European** digital design and manufacturing processes, which could benefit indigenous projects like **TAPAS-BH-201**.
 
 
 
• **Context of Other Options:**
 
 
• **nEUROn**: This is an experimental **unmanned combat aerial vehicle (UCAV)** developed by **Dassault Aviation** focused on **stealth** technology.
 
• **Global Hawk**: A **High-Altitude Long-Endurance (HALE)** platform produced by **Northrop Grumman** in the **United States**.
 
• **Predator XP**: An export variant of the **MQ-1 Predator** drone manufactured by **General Atomics**; it is an older generation system compared to the current **MQ-9B** series.
